extracted.intended_audience: EPA-regulated facilities/operators, state permitting authorities, environmental consultants, and public commenters on CCR rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts and explains the regulatory criteria EPA uses in the preamble to (1) define 'CCR management unit' (CCRMU), (2) determine applicability and thresholds for regulation, and (3) evaluate damage cases, monitoring data, and alternative source demonstrations (ASDs) for groundwater impacts from CCR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance of documented damage cases even if remediated
rubrics_metrics.description: Cases where contamination has been remediated remain relevant to this rulemaking; facts demonstrating consequences from particular activities remain relevant, particularly (although not solely) where the management practices continue to occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA will rely on damage cases to evaluate the extent and nature of risks associated with CCR management practices. What matters are facts that provide information on the reasons that unit leaked, the particular contaminants that were present, the levels of those contaminants, and the nature of any impacts caused by that contamination. The fact that contamination has subsequently been remediated is not a basis for disregarding a damage case; this is consistent with RCRA section 8002(n)'s requirement to evaluate potential danger in addition to documented damage cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of damage cases to validate risk modeling and demonstrate management-practice consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Damage cases provide 'real world' evidence against which to compare EPA's risk modeling estimates and provide direct evidence regarding specific waste management practices and their potential consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA uses damage cases to assess frequency of constituent leaching into groundwater and to inform regulatory decisions; the Agency expects additional damage cases will be discovered with expanded groundwater monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of units showing groundwater contamination regardless of State oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Data from units shows CCRMU are contributing to groundwater contamination, irrespective of any prior State oversight; such units should not be excluded from consideration simply because they were regulated under State programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA disagrees with commenters that damage cases are not representative of CCRMU because State programs had oversight; presence of contamination is dispositive for inclusion in the record of relevant damage cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'CCR management unit' (CCRMU)
rubrics_metrics.description: CCRMU defined as any area of land on which any non-containerized accumulations of CCR are received, placed, or otherwise managed, that is not a CCR unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The definition is based on existing definitions of CCR pile and CCR surface impoundment and explicitly includes historical solid waste management units such as CCR landfills and surface impoundments that closed prior to October 19, 2015, as well as inactive CCR landfills (including abandoned piles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability thresholds for part 257, subpart D regulation of CCRMU
rubrics_metrics.description: §257.50(d) revised to specify that part 257, subpart D applies to CCRMU of 1,000 tons or greater located at facilities with a regulated CCR unit or active facilities without a regulated CCR unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CCR management units greater than or equal to one ton and less than 1,000 tons located at active facilities (or legacy CCR surface impoundments, per text) are subject only to the FER in §257.75 until a permitting authority determines that regulation of these units, individually or aggregated, is warranted and determines the applicable requirements. This amends the 2015 CCR Rule exemption for landfills that ceased receiving CCR prior to October 19, 2015.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural effect of a successful ASD for Appendix IV SSLs
rubrics_metrics.description: Under existing CCR regulations, when a facility determines there is an SSL for one or more Appendix IV constituents and completes a successful Alternative Source Demonstration (ASD) showing that a source other than the regulated unit is the cause of the SSL(s), the facility is not required to initiate corrective action for that particular constituent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA reviews ASDs posted on facility websites; if the ASD credibly attributes an SSL to another source (e.g., adjacent unregulated impoundment), the regulated unit need not remediate that constituent under the Federal CCR regulations. EPA nonetheless evaluates the totality of evidence in the damage cases record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural effect of a successful ASD for Appendix III SSIs
rubrics_metrics.description: When a facility determines there is a Statistically Significant Increase (SSI) for one or more Appendix III constituents and completes a successful ASD showing an alternative source, the facility is not required to initiate assessment monitoring for that constituent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA's ASD reviews identified areas where CCR was managed outside regulated units and was identified as the source of one or more Appendix III SSIs; in such cases, units have remained in detection monitoring rather than moving to assessment monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence required to evaluate damage cases and source attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA looks for facts that explain why a unit leaked, which contaminants were present, contaminant concentrations, and the nature of any impacts; adequate groundwater monitoring is necessary to characterize impacts and determine whether an unregulated placement is a CCRMU or a damage case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where monitoring wells are insufficient (sparse, improperly located, or lacking network coverage), neither EPA nor commenters can definitively determine whether the placement is a CCRMU or a damage case. ASDs and determinations attributing SSIs/SSLs to historic or alternative sources must be supported by analysis that evaluates potential sources (e.g., upgradient wells, borings, historic fill data).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of SSIs and SSLs as triggers for further action
rubrics_metrics.description: Detection of SSIs (statistically significant increases above background for Appendix III constituents) and SSLs (exceedances of groundwater protection standards for Appendix IV constituents) indicate potential releases and guide whether facilities must move from detection monitoring to assessment monitoring or corrective action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA examples show that identification of SSIs/SSLs has led to ASDs, assessments of corrective measures, and selected remedies (e.g., source removal and final cover). Whether a facility must proceed to assessment or corrective action depends on monitoring results and the adequacy/credibility of any ASD attributing the SSI/SSL to another source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of historical CCR placement and use of CCR as fill
rubrics_metrics.description: Historical CCR placed as fill, CCR buried near ponds, or construction using CCR (e.g., berms, ramps, quarry fills) can be sources of groundwater contamination and should be considered when interpreting monitoring data and attributing sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA notes examples where borings and construction drawings show CCR in berms or fill near monitoring wells; monitoring networks that place upgradient wells within the footprint of historical CCR make source attribution unreliable. ASDs that attribute SSIs/SSLs to historic fill should analyze these potential sources to verify claims; failure to analyze leaves uncertainty and may warrant regulation of the CCRMU.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitting authority discretion for smaller CCRMU
rubrics_metrics.description: For CCRMU between 1 ton and less than 1,000 tons located at active facilities or legacy surface impoundments, regulation may be limited to the FER in §257.75 until a permitting authority determines regulation of these units (individually or aggregated) is warranted and determines applicable requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives permitting authorities the discretion to evaluate whether smaller or aggregated units should be regulated beyond the FER; facilities cannot rely automatically on the pre-2015 exemption for units that ceased receiving CCR before October 19, 2015.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA reliance standard for damage-case veracity
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA has sufficient confidence in the veracity of collected damage-case information to rely on it for rulemaking decisions when the information documents contamination and management practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA expects additional cases will be identified through expanded monitoring; while EPA accepts remediation does not negate evidentiary value, it evaluates the reliability and representativeness of each damage case in context (e.g., whether monitoring was adequate, whether ASDs are well-supported).
